newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Kwasniewski says tax cut too deep.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Kwasniewski says tax cut too deep.

text.p: President Aleksander Kwasniewski criticised a sharp tax cut which parliament unexpectedly imposed on Poland's horrified prime minister on Thursday, saying that it went too far.

"If we can have lower taxes let's do it, but this must not destroy the economy and it cannot slow down the economic growth we are praised for," Kwasniewski told Polish television during a visit to London.

The lower house voted to throw out government plans for a moderate cut in personal income taxes to 20, 31 and 43 percent from 21, 33 and 45 percent and to replace the current scale with a new scale of 17, 20, 33 and 45 percent.
"I don't know whether the 17 percent scale is realistic. In my opinion it is going too far and I fully back government tax cut proposals for 1997," Kwasniewski said.

Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz and Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said the unexpected move would slash revenues and seriously disrupt carefully-laid plans for the 1997 budget, due to be presented to parliament next week.

The new tax scale was passed, against the wishes of Cimoszewicz's main ruling Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), by its smaller coalition partner the Polish Peasant party voting along with opposition deputies.
Former SLD leader Kwasniewski's views on it are especially relevant as the president can veto bills and send them back to parliament for a new vote.
The SLD has said it will use all legal means to block the new 17 percent tax level, which could involve calling on the president to use his veto.
